coverageNote: Enumeration matches the expected 5 units / 33 files exactly. Units: the domain directory itself (education-lessons-mentorship-index.md + -cx.md + the 7 flat leaf features 06.05-06.11 = 9 files) and the four sub-domain directories 06.01 (6 files), 06.02 (6), 06.03 (7), 06.04 (5). Every file was read in full. Dimension 5 (Success Measurability) and Dimension 6 (Competitive Positioning) are scored N/A for the four sub-domain units: product success metrics and named-competitor positioning are owned at vision/meta and domain-index level in this tree, and the domain-root unit carries both (4 named competitors + a defensible moat; Q-08 resolves domain measurability explicitly). Scoring them at sub-domain level would penalise those units for content that is deliberately not theirs.

findings.claim: The both-parties-no-show ledger outcome is specified two incompatible ways with no marker on either: the credit-ledger owner says the credit sits in limbo pending an open question, while the policy owner records that same question as RESOLVED with the credit returning immediately.
findings.evidence: 06.01.02-lesson-packages-credits-rate-cards.md:223 (edge case 35): "Both parties no-show | The ledger will not burn without a resolved earning event. The credit sits in **limbo**, un-consumed and un-returned, pending 06.01.03's rule (their Q-03)." — contradicted by 06.01.03-cancellation-makeup-no-show-policy.md:268 (Q-03): "~~Both-parties-no-show: who eats it?~~ **RESOLVED** -> DT-09 / D-11. Nobody eats it: the credit returns, no signal on either party, both are asked whether the lesson moved" and 06.01.03-cancellation-makeup-no-show-policy.md:144: "Nobody joins a remote lesson | Grace elapses; **both-no-show** rule fires (D-03) — credit returns, no signal either side". 06.01.04-lesson-delivery-session-record.md:246 repeats the stale reading: "Both parties no-show (remote) | ... the ledger effect is 06.01.03's open Q-03 and is deliberately not decided here".
findings.forcedInvention: An implementer must invent the ledger outcome for a both-no-show occurrence: hold the credit in an un-returned limbo state (per the ledger owner, 06.01.02, which also requires a limbo state to exist in the ledger's state machine) or return it immediately with no signal (per the policy owner, 06.01.03, whose question is closed). The two answers differ in money position, in the states the ledger must model, and in whether a dispute path is entered.
findings.quotedSecondary: 06.01.03's own edge rows attribute the both-no-show rule to '(D-03)', but 06.01.03 D-03 is "A teacher with no policy gets the **platform default preset**, labelled as such" — the both-no-show rule has no decision row of its own, and the Empty state cites a non-existent "D-03-original".

findings.claim: Safeguarding vetting is required to render as a 'badge' with status grammar on the two highest-traffic surfaces (public profile, result card) by two sibling features, while the feature that owns the credential block bans exactly that rendering and calls it the most dangerous design in the file.
findings.evidence: 06.02.01-teacher-tuition-profile.md:124 (D-09 tier table): "**Public, indexed** (no account) | Identity header; ... credential **claims** and badges (\"played bass on {record}\"; \"DBS checked, current\"); reviews; rate ..." and 06.02.01-teacher-tuition-profile.md:32 (Fan Role Lens): "Sees: identity header, all self-authored and structured tuition content, credential **claims** and badges". 06.02.03-teacher-discovery-match-criteria.md:162 (Happy Path 5): "Each card states its top two reasons in plain language, the rate in the viewer's currency, next availability as a **shape** (signed-out), a vetting badge, and the evidence mix from 06.02.02"; also :223 (Populated state) "vetting badge" and :197 "Nobody sees a stale vetting badge". Contradicted by 06.02.02-verified-credentials-credit-backed-credibility.md:313 (D-11): "Vetting renders as a **dated statement naming the check and its jurisdiction**, never as a badge, tick or shield"; :161 "No green tick. No shield. No word \"safe\"."; :270 (DT-07) "Vetting can be rendered as a verified badge ... ❌ REJECTED, and this is the most dangerous design in the file ... **A tick is status grammar; the fact is a snapshot.**"; :304 (D-02) "no composite trust score, **no summary badge, no headline count**". The parent index agrees with 06.02.02: 06.02-teacher-discovery-profiles-trials-index.md:41 says the Fan sees "each credit as a plain sentence with its record and role ... **never a badge** (D-02)".
findings.forcedInvention: An implementer must invent the public rendering of the safeguarding signal: a compact 'DBS checked, current' badge (06.02.01 D-09's own worked example and 06.02.03's card spec, which is the only thing that fits a result card) or a dated multi-clause statement naming the check, jurisdiction, date and its limits (06.02.02 D-11). The phrase 'current' is itself the status grammar 06.02.02 DT-07 rejects, because the platform cannot know a check is current after its issue date without the opt-in UK Update Service.

findings.claim: 06.01.04 states two mutually exclusive 'regardless' rules for the same occurrence: crossing 50% concurrent presence makes it delivered regardless of what happens next, and an audio-quality drop lets it end with no credit consumed regardless of the 50% rule.
findings.evidence: 06.01.04-lesson-delivery-session-record.md:192 (Happy Path 7): "Concurrent presence crosses **50%** of the scheduled duration -> the occurrence is `delivered` **regardless of what happens next**" and :88 (D-06 predicate) "**Delivered** | Concurrent server-stamped presence >= **50%** of the occurrence's scheduled duration | `delivered` — 06.01.02 consumes the reserved credit". Contradicted by :229: "Audio quality falls below the music-fidelity floor for >60s | ... offered: continue at speech quality ..., or end with **no credit consumed** regardless of the 50% rule". This also breaches the file's own seam statement at :24: "It never decides a ledger effect — 06.01.03 does that" and D-06's "**This feature emits facts; 06.01.03 decides ledger effects.**"
findings.forcedInvention: For a 30-minute lesson where both parties were present for 20 minutes and then audio degraded below the floor, the implementer must decide whether the credit consumes (delivery predicate already satisfied, irreversibly) or returns (degradation escape hatch), and whether 06.01.04 or 06.01.03 owns that ledger decision. 06.01.03 has no rule for audio degradation; its nearest mapping is D-16's 'platform-caused -> no-fault', which would contradict the delivered-regardless invariant.

findings.claim: Whether a WeJammin certificate may render on the same surface as verified credits is answered both ways, and 06.08 cites as its authority the very rejected-pair row that permits what 06.08 forbids.
findings.evidence: 06.02-teacher-discovery-profiles-trials/06.02-teacher-discovery-profiles-trials-cx.md:176 (R-02): "Considered rendering WeJammin-issued certificates in the credential block alongside verified credits. Rejected at this level: ... **They may co-render; they must not merge.**" (and 06.02.02:294 restates it: "Per sub-domain R-02 they may co-render; they must not merge"). Contradicted by 06.08-certificates-badges-verification.md:101 (D-03): "Certificates must **never** render beside verified credits, nor feed the credential block" and education-lessons-mentorship-cx.md:20 (CX-09): "Certificates must **never** render beside verified credits — debasement by association". 06.08:60 then attributes its own stricter rule to the permissive row: "Learner displays it beside verified credits (06.02.02) | **Actively harmful.** ... | 06.02 CX R-02 rejects the co-render for exactly this reason" — R-02 does not reject the co-render, it permits it.
findings.forcedInvention: An implementer must decide whether a certificate artifact may appear on a page that also renders the credential block (permitted, visually separated, per 06.02 R-02) or must be excluded from that surface entirely (per 06.08 D-03 and domain CX-09). Following 06.08's citation leads to a row that states the opposite of the rule citing it.

findings.claim: The domain CX assigns two substantive academy powers to decisions 06.10 D-06 and 06.10 D-11, neither of which exists — 06.10 has only D-01 to D-04 — and one of the claims (a same-day remedy on every in-flight series when a building closes) is stated nowhere in any owning file.
findings.evidence: education-lessons-mentorship-cx.md:151: "floor cancellation policy (bounds what teachers can undercut — Step 5 resolves its ambiguous direction: it is a **ceiling on harshness, not a mandate**; teachers may always be more generous, 06.01.03 -> 06.10 D-06)" and :153: "A fifth binding surfaced in Step 5: the **no-fault closure cascade** — closing the building (06.10 D-11) forces the same-day remedy on every in-flight series with no notice period, because the room is gone." 06.10-academy-multi-teacher-operations.md contains exactly four decisions (:110-:113): D-01 academy is an Operator, D-02 organisation entity + teaching-operations layer, D-03 student belongs to the academy / identity to the teacher, D-04 the academy layer is optional and invisible. The nearest real decisions are 06.01.03 D-06 ("The academy floor is a **ceiling on harshness**, not a mandate") and 06.01.03 D-11 ("**No-fault** is a first-class settlement class ... Operator closure cascades automatically to every lesson in the affected rooms") — but 06.01.03 D-11's cascade returns the credit per affected lesson with no signal; it says nothing about a same-day remedy on a series. The only 'same-day remedy' in the tree is 06.01.02's involuntary teacher-departure flow (:153: "**Involuntary** ... **no notice**, remedy flow opens the same day"), which is triggered by a teacher leaving, not by a room closing. 06.10's own edge row for closure (:70) points somewhere else again: "Academy closes with credits outstanding | ... | 06.01.02 Q-01/Q-02" (an open question).
findings.forcedInvention: For an Operator closing a building, an implementer must invent whether the effect is (a) per-lesson no-fault settlement for the affected occurrences (06.01.03 D-11), (b) opening 06.01.02's reassign/refund/transfer remedy flow same-day against every in-flight series (domain CX-05), or (c) nothing until 06.01.02 Q-01/Q-02 is answered (06.10's edge row). Following the cited authority resolves nothing because the cited decisions do not exist.

findings.claim: The no-show grace formula is illustrated with a lesson duration the rate card cannot express, leaving it undecidable whether sub-30-minute occurrences exist.
findings.evidence: 06.01.03-cancellation-makeup-no-show-policy.md:83: "**At `scheduled_start + grace`** — the no-show evaluation. `grace = min(15 min, 50% x duration)`, floor 5 min. **A 20-minute beginner's lesson gets 10 minutes, not 15.**" But 06.01.02-lesson-packages-credits-rate-cards.md:28 closes the duration set: "one line per (instrument x duration x mode x level), where duration in {30, 45, 60, 90 min}", and 06.01.02 D-07 pins a credit to a rate-card line. Under that enum the minimum grace is min(15, 15) = 15 minutes for every bookable occurrence, so both the worked example and the 5-minute floor are unreachable.
findings.forcedInvention: An implementer must decide whether durations outside {30,45,60,90} are bookable (making the grace formula's variable branch and its 5-minute floor live) or whether the enum is closed (making them dead code and the quoted example wrong). The answer also determines whether 06.01.01's slot-length options are open-ended, since its availability rule example lists "30/45/60-min slots" without stating the set is closed.

findings.claim: Two sibling features define a series state with the same name, 'At Risk', on different triggers, and the ledger owner claims ownership of the timing while the calendar owner fixes the trigger at zero balance.
findings.evidence: 06.01.02-lesson-packages-credits-rate-cards.md:141: "When available credits reach **<= 2**, or when reserved occurrences would exhaust the balance within **21 days** at the series' cadence — whichever fires first — the ledger raises an **at-risk** signal on the series and prompts a top-up. **This feature owns the signal and its timing.**" and its States table :239: "| At risk | Available <= 2, or reserved occurrences exhaust the balance within 21 days | ...". Against 06.01.01-lesson-slot-booking-recurring-series.md:162: "| **At Risk** | Balance 0, next occurrence unreserved | Student: amber series + \"Top up by 30 Jul to keep Tuesday 17:00\" ..." and D-03 (:230): "Zero balance -> At Risk (slot held) for 2 occurrences or 14 days -> Lapsed".
findings.forcedInvention: An implementer must decide whether a series with 2 credits remaining renders as At Risk (06.01.02's trigger, on the surface where the amber state and the release date live) or only at zero (06.01.01's trigger, which is also where the grace clock starts) — i.e. whether there is one state with two triggers or two states sharing a name.

But 06.01.01's Q-01 (:244) is "**Can a student register interest in a teacher with no open slots?**", and 06.01.01 D-03 (:230) explicitly decides the suspend/release question: "Also answers sub-domain **CX-06** (`[PARTIAL]` — does a zero balance suspend or release?): both, in that order, with a stated date." Whether a zero balance **suspends** ... or **releases** ... is unresolved" with "**Role scoping**: `[PENDING — /ideate-discover Step 5]`, pending Q-02" — and the CX file contains no Q-02, though CX-01 (:38) also refers to one: "the Teacher is notified of the forward-book risk to their standing slot only if Q-02 below resolves to release".

findings.claim: The credit lifecycle state machine lets a lapsed credit transition straight to consumed on redemption, bypassing the reserved state that the sub-domain's fail-closed reservation invariant depends on.
findings.evidence: 06.01.02-lesson-packages-credits-rate-cards.md:75-79 ("**Credit lifecycle** — the ledger's state machine"): "granted --reserve (06.01.01 confirm)--> reserved" ... "lapsed --redeem at current list--> consumed  (student tops up the delta)". Every other path to consumed runs through reserved, and the reservation step is what enforces the sub-domain's core invariant, stated at :20: "no operation can drive negative or double-count — one lesson's credit is spent once and only once", with CX-01 Q2 requiring "Booking confirmation -> reserve. If the reserve fails (insufficient balance), the **booking must fail** — fail closed". D-04 (:288) describes redemption as booking-time behaviour ("redeemable against the teacher's current list price with the student topping up any delta"), which implies a reservation.
findings.forcedInvention: An implementer must decide whether redeeming a lapsed credit re-enters the normal reserve-then-consume flow (and therefore whether a residual can be double-booked against two occurrences) or consumes directly as the diagram states, which would bypass the single-writer reservation guard for exactly the credits that carry a cash residual.

findings.claim: 06.01.02 twice routes the over-run question to '06.01.04 Q-04', but 06.01.04's Q-04 now asks about interrupted-lesson compensation; the over-run question was absorbed into D-05, which still claims to resolve 'Q-04'.
findings.evidence: 06.01.02-lesson-packages-credits-rate-cards.md:82: "an over-running lesson (06.01.04 Q-04) burns zero or one additional credit, never a fraction" and :271: "Its Q-04 (over-run) is bounded here". But 06.01.04-lesson-delivery-session-record.md:383 (Q-04) reads: "**Does the platform compensate the teacher for an `interrupted` lesson?**", and D-05 (:362) says "**Over-run is free** ... | Per DT-14, resolving Q-04" — i.e. two different questions are called Q-04 in one file, one of them closed.
findings.forcedInvention: A reader following the pointer to settle over-run behaviour lands on an unrelated open question about transport-fault compensation, and cannot tell whether over-run is decided (D-05: free, hard-stopped by the next commitment, no second charge) or still open.

findings.claim: 06.03.05's body defers the skill model to the completed /ideate-discover Step 5 run, while the same file's Q-02 records that question as resolved in the negative and D-03 ratifies the consequence.
findings.evidence: 06.03.05-progress-reports-skill-tracking.md:37: "`[PENDING — /ideate-discover Step 5]`: the skill model itself. Whether ability is representable at all beyond exam-board grades (06.09) and a teacher's prose is genuinely unresolved, and inventing a skill taxonomy at breadth would be fabrication." Contradicted by the same file's Q-02 (:106): "~~Is there any honest skill model beyond exam grades and a teacher's prose?~~ **RESOLVED — no, there is not.**" and D-03 (:98): "The platform measures **coverage**, never **musicianship**". The stage named is documented as complete throughout the tree (e.g. 06.03-...-index.md:86: "re-pointed from the completed `/ideate-discover` Step 5 run").
findings.forcedInvention: A reader who stops at the Behavior section believes a skill taxonomy is still to be designed for a feature whose name is 'Skill Tracking', when the resolved position is that no such model may be claimed beyond coverage, an exam grade and the teacher's prose.
